chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Abdullah ibn 'Amir from 'Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from al-Qasim ibn Burayd from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who stands in prayer during the last part of the night, fearing that dawn will overtake him: should he begin with the Witr prayer, or should he pray the night prayer in its proper form until the Witr becomes the final part of that? He said, 'Rather, he should begin with the Witr.' And he said, 'I used to do that.'.
And if he prays four rak'ahs of the night prayer, and then dawn overtakes him, it is permissible for him to complete the night prayer and then pray the Fajr (morning) prayer; this indicates that.

key_terms.الْوَتْر: Witr, the odd-numbered prayer performed at the end of the night

ai.seo_question: What is the correct order of prayers if one fears dawn will arrive while praying night prayers?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the precedence of Witr when time is short, a ruling he personally practiced, reflecting the Shia emphasis on Witr as a confirmed Sunnah rather than merely a closing act. This guidance ensures the preservation of the distinct Witr prayer even under the pressure of Fajr's onset, while allowing flexibility for those already engaged in night prayer to complete their voluntary acts before the obligatory dawn prayer.
